div.div: Q. 1 دَمْلَجَ , (JM, TA,) inf. n. دَمْلَجَةٌ and دِمْلَاجٌ, (K, TA,) He made, or wrought, a thing, (K, JM, TA,) as, for instance, a bracelet, (TA,) evenly or equably, or justly or properly, (K, JM, TA,) and well. (JM, TA.) [And He made a thing round and smooth; like دَمْلَقَهُ: see the pass. part. n., below.] It is said in a trad., دَمْلَجَ ٱللّٰهُ لُؤْلُؤَهُ [God has made his pearls round and smooth]. (TA.) Accord. to Lh, دُمْلِجَ جِسْمُهُ signifies His body was, or became, rounded, or compacted, (طُوِىَ,) so that his, or its, flesh was firm, or hard. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
